plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Waystream switch. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory utilization, temperature, and interface traffic, for ASR and FTTH access switches (enterprise PEN 9303).
name: Switch

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: CPU utilization of the Waystream switch control plane (PEN 9303 wsSystem). Prefer 100 minus wsCPUIdleLoad; if idle is absent, fall back to wsCPUUserLoad plus wsCPUSystemLoad. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload, routing instability, or attack traffic, and may lead to slow management response or packet processing delays.

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: Used system memory of the Waystream switch in bytes (wsMemoryUsed, reported in kilobytes and multiplied by 1024). Helps administrators see absolute memory consumption and identify memory pressure.

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: Total system memory of the Waystream switch in bytes (wsMemoryTotal, reported in kilobytes and multiplied by 1024). Together with used bytes it is the denominator for memory utilization.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Overall memory utilization of the Waystream switch. Prefer used / total from wsMemoryUsed and wsMemoryTotal; if those scalars are absent, fall back to 100 minus wsMemoryPctFree after dividing tenths of a percent by 10. High memory usage may indicate memory leaks, oversized tables, or insufficient capacity.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Highest chassis temperature reading from the optional wsTempMeasured table, in degrees Celsius. The raw object is hundredths of a degree, so the query divides by 100. Models without this table simply omit the metric. Abnormally high temperatures may indicate cooling failure, blocked airflow, or excessive ambient heat.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
